title: It's September 1. Howie Roseman did not make a trade in August. He has not made a trade since June 1. Last year, he made 6 trades between 8/5 and 9/9. Why the inactivity? Roseman: "I think from our perspective, a lot of conversations with every team — almost every team; there's a couple, maybe not so much — but I think that when we were talking to these other teams, the players they were interested in, felt like we were going to hold on to. The players maybe we were interested in, maybe they felt the same way. With the way that practices went and the games went, there wasn't an opportunity to do some of the player-for-player trades. We like to get looks at guys just because of where our numbers were. I think you guys know me well enough to know that I like the action and was trying, but it just didn't make sense for us at the time. We would've just been doing it to make a move."

title: The Eagles have signed RB Jaydon Blue to the practice squad, according to ESPN. Some thoughts on the signing: ** I think this is a player worth using a practice squad spot on. Blue was a 5th-round pick just last year. The Eagles clearly liked him as a draft prospect, bringing him in for a top-30 visit. Now they get him in their building just a year later on a practice squad spot. ** Blue was an intriguing prospect out of Texas because he showed the ability to be a threat out of the backfield. Blue caught 56 passes for 9 YPC and 7 TDs, including six his final year. ** Blue ran an impressive 4.28 and 4.29 in the 40 ** It didn’t work out in Dallas, with Blue carrying the ball only 38 times and getting one target in the passing game. He also returned three kicks for 72 yards. ** It won’t be easy to get onto the 53-man roster at the RB spot with Barkley, Bigsby and Shipley ahead of him, but Blue’s ability to be a pass-catching back plus return kicks might get him elevated for a game sooner rather than later.

** Blue ran an impressive 4.28 and 4.29 in the 40

** It didn’t work out in Dallas, with Blue carrying the ball only 38 times and getting one target in the passing game. He also returned three kicks for 72 yards. 

** It won’t be easy to get onto the 53-man roster at the RB spot with Barkley, Bigsby and Shipley ahead of him, but Blue’s ability to be a pass-catching back plus return kicks might get him elevated for a game sooner rather than later.

title: Howie Roseman on the O-line depth: "I don't know if we talked about this before camp, but certainly if any of you would've given me a truth serum and said, 'What are you looking for in training camp?' It would be how our interior offensive line depth panned out and the way that Drew (Kendall), Willie (Lampkin), and then obviously Micah (Morris), keeping Micah. Those young guys and the growth that they showed, their ability to play in the passing game, in the run game. "...Really, really excited about those guys, about being able to have those guys, being able to develop those guys, but at the same time, have confidence that if those guys need to play, that they're ready to play. I was saying it, our interior O-Line depth, it was kind of in a different spot than it had been in years past, relying on some young guys to take a step. A lot of credit to (chris) Kuper and the guys around him for getting these guys ready to go. Feel like we're in a really good spot there and it was a concern going into camp."

title: Howie Roseman on waiving Bernard/Weru: “I don't know that there's a comfort level in exposing anyone. We're not sitting there and cutting anyone and going, 'Woohoo, this guy, we're definitely getting back.' You don't know what other teams are thinking. We put a lot of time and effort during this week, not only to looking at what's going to be out there, but by taking snapshots of what other teams are seeing in our guys, and saying, 'They don't have the practices, they don't have the individual periods, they don't have these guys in the meeting rooms just like we don't when we're looking at other guys.' Going back and watching the tape and just evaluating the tape and what other teams are seeing, and that's not an exact science. Certainly didn't want to get four guys claimed. That doesn't feel great. But from our perspective, development is real. These guys have tremendous ability to be developed. They want to be developed. They have tools in their body, they've got great character, but it's new to them. “I think that Jordan (Mailata), with all due respect to Joshua and Uar -- I don't know, whoever's the youngest person in this room probably could be doing this for 30, 40 years, and nobody's going to see a Jordan Mailata ever again. I mean the person, the player that that guy is, that story, it's an unbelievable story. He had just a unique combination of size, strength, athleticism and pro experience as an athlete. I think sometimes we forget Uar has never played organized sports before. It's a different bar. I think if we're just judging everyone through the lens of Jordan Mailata, it's going to be hard to give these guys a fair chance. Still very excited about them, really glad that they did get through. Certainly wasn't certain about that, but I'm glad they're back here.”

title: Howie Roseman on keeping 4 QBs: “Four quarterbacks, the most important position in sports. I feel like all those guys have value for our team. Obviously, some is short-term value, some is long-term value when you think about Cole [Payton]. As we went through the process here, just thought it was the right thing to do for our football team. “…It’s just such a valuable position. From our perspective, last year, obviously we took someone in the fifth round, let him go. He left our practice squad to go somewhere else, traded for a sixth-round pick. These guys are valuable. They take time to develop at the same time. That position is so valuable to this organization over a long period of time. [We] want to be strong there and think both those guys behind Jalen [Hurts] have value, have shown that over the course of their careers. We kind of take all the information at our disposal to make all these decisions.”

They thought he did a good job standing in the pocket and delivering the ball. "He's not afraid to rip it" and "made a lot of big time throws." They didn't want to risk losing him.
